parent.none: Not attached to a parent ticket.

customers.title: Customers
customers.name: Name
customers.newDomainsHint: Separate several domains with spaces or commas. Mail from a registered domain opens tickets for the customer.
import.title: Import customers, sites, requesters and assets
import.intro: Customers, their sites, their requesters and their assets come from CSV files in UTF-8, one file per kind, separated by commas or semicolons, with fixed column names in the first row. A customer is recognised by its external reference, else by its name; a site by its name within its customer; a requester by any of their e-mail addresses; an asset by its serial number within its customer, else by its name. A filled cell sets a value, an empty one leaves it. An import never deletes, retires or offboards anything, never marks a requester departed, and never changes an asset an add-on is the source of.
import.filesHint: The customers file is taken first, then the sites file, then the requesters file, then the assets file, so that a row can refer to a customer, site or requester an earlier file creates. Nothing changes until you import; the import checks every row again.
import.filesHintWithoutAssets: The customers file is taken first, then the sites file, then the requesters file, so that a row can refer to a customer or site an earlier file creates. Importing assets needs managing the catalog too. Nothing changes until you import; the import checks every row again.
import.previewed: This is a preview: nothing has changed yet.
import.applied: Imported. The rows left out were not.
import.notUtf8: {file} is not in UTF-8. Save it as “CSV UTF-8” and choose it again.
import.tooLarge: The files are too large for one import. Split them into several imports.
import.leftOutHint: They have the same columns and an error column with the reason: correct them and import the file again.
customer.name: Name
customer.taxIdHint: A tax identifier, such as a VAT number, always comes with the country that issued it.
customer.notesHint: Only agents see the notes; they are never sent to the customer.
customer.offboardedNotice: Offboarded on {date}. Its history stays, but it gets no new tickets: every message from its requesters and domains waits in the inbox.
customer.domainsHint: Mail from an unknown sender at one of these domains opens a ticket for this customer and registers the sender as a requester.
customer.keyRequestersHint: Key requesters speak for the customer: they get the replies on its tickets that have no requester, and the messages about failures that affect it, at the address chosen here.
customer.offboardHint: An offboarded customer keeps its history but gets no new tickets; its mail waits in the inbox.
customer.confirmOffboard: Offboard {name}? Its history stays, but it gets no new tickets: every message from its requesters and domains, replies included, will wait in the inbox, until it is brought back.
customer.bringBackHint: Brought back, the customer gets tickets again: messages from its requesters and domains open them, and it is offered when opening tickets. Messages that waited in the inbox stay there to be sorted.
customer.confirmBringBack: Bring {name} back? It keeps its history, requesters and assets, and from now on messages from its requesters and domains open tickets again.
requester.name: Name
requester.notesHint: Only agents see the notes; they are never sent to the requester.
requester.addressesHint: Mail from any of these addresses identifies the requester.
requester.departedNotice: This requester has left the customer. Their history stays, but no ticket is opened for them, and every message from their addresses, replies included, waits in the inbox.
requester.noAddresses: No addresses left: the ones they kept passed to the requester they became at another customer.
requester.departHint: A requester who leaves the customer is marked departed and keeps their history; the assets they hold lose their holder. Someone who moves to another customer becomes a new requester there, and the addresses they keep pass to it.
requester.confirmDepart: Mark {name} as departed? Their history stays, but no ticket is opened for them, and every message from their addresses, replies included, waits in the inbox. They can come back.

requester.confirmDepartWithAssets.one: Mark {name} as departed? Their history stays, but no ticket is opened for them, and every message from their addresses, replies included, waits in the inbox. The asset they hold, {assets}, loses its holder. They can come back.
requester.confirmDepartWithAssets.other: Mark {name} as departed? Their history stays, but no ticket is opened for them, and every message from their addresses, replies included, waits in the inbox. The {count} assets they hold lose their holder: {assets}. They can come back.

requester.comeBackHint: A departed requester can come back: their messages open and follow tickets again.
requester.comeBackNeedsAddress: To come back, the requester needs an address of their own: add one above first.
requester.mergeHint: If another requester of {customer} is the same person, merge them into this one: their addresses, tickets and the assets they hold pass to this requester, and they are removed. Requesters of different customers are never merged.
requester.mergeWith: Requester to merge into this one
requester.noneToMerge: {customer} has no other requester to merge with this one.
requester.confirmMerge: Merge {other} into {name}? The addresses, tickets and held assets of {other} pass to {name}, and {other} is removed. A merge cannot be undone.
requester.moveHint: If this requester was identified with the wrong customer, move them to the right one. All their tickets move with them, closed ones included.

requester.moveTakesTickets.other: All their {count} tickets move with them, closed ones included.

requester.moveNoTickets: They have no tickets to move.
requester.moveLeavesSite: They leave their site, {site}, which belongs to {customer}.
requester.moveEndsKeyRequester: They stop being a key requester of {customer}.

requester.moveLeavesAssets.one: The asset they hold, {assets}, stays with {customer} without a holder.
requester.moveLeavesAssets.other: The {count} assets they hold stay with {customer} without a holder: {assets}.

sites.hint: Where the customer's requesters and assets are. A retired site stays visible but gets no new requesters or assets.
sites.name: Site name
sites.confirmRetire: Retire {name}? It stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.

sites.confirmRetireWithRequesters.one: Retire {name}? {requesters} is at it and will be left without a site. The site stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.
sites.confirmRetireWithRequesters.other: Retire {name}? {count} requesters are at it and will be left without a site: {requesters}. The site stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.

sites.confirmRetireWithAssets.other: Retire {name}? {count} assets will lose this site: {assets}. The site stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.

sites.confirmRetireWithRequesterAndAsset.one: Retire {name}? {requesters} is at it and will be left without a site, and the asset {assets} will lose this site. The site stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.
sites.confirmRetireWithRequesterAndAsset.other: Retire {name}? {requesters} is at it and will be left without a site, and {count} assets will lose this site: {assets}. The site stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.

sites.confirmRetireWithRequestersAndAsse.one: Retire {name}? {requesterCount} requesters are at it and will be left without a site: {requesters}; and the asset {assets} will lose this site. The site stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.
sites.confirmRetireWithRequestersAndAsse.other: Retire {name}? {requesterCount} requesters are at it and will be left without a site: {requesters}; and {count} assets will lose this site: {assets}. The site stays visible, but no requester or asset can be put at it any more.

assets.confirmRetireHeld: Retire {name}? It stays on the tickets that refer to it, but no ticket or service can link it any more, and {holder} no longer holds it.
assets.suppliedHint: An asset from an add-on changes in the add-on's system, which retires it when it leaves; here it only gets a holder.

agents.confirmReset: Reset the password of {name}? They are signed out everywhere and need the new password, shown once, to sign in again.
